extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians and comedy writers seeking to write/perform clean, anecdotal, befuddled-narrator style material (family-friendly/club/TV sets)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and performing clean, observational, anecdotal stand-up in the 'befuddled narrator' school exemplified by Brian Regan — emphasizes universal mundane topics, physicality, and story-shaped jokes with clean language. Includes performance notes (body language, facial punctuation, voice) and micro-structure (setup/complication/punch/tag).

rubrics_metrics.name: Befuddled anecdotal narrator (self-deprecating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the comedian the befuddled narrator (self-deprecating)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The performer adopts a bumbling, confused narrator persona who is the butt of the joke rather than attacking others; self-deprecation is central. This ties to the 'school of befuddled anecdotal narrators.' Anti-pattern: a confident, one-upper persona or mean-spirited targeting of others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic selection: universal and mundane
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the topic universal and mundane?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose everyday subjects that a broad audience recognizes (examples given: shipping a package with UPS, mortgages, optometrist visits, doughnut decisions, trampoline). Avoid niche, insider, or highly political topics. The aim is recognition pleasure rather than exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational — sees the absurd in the ordinary
rubrics_metrics.description: Observational — sees the absurd in the ordinary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material should highlight the small absurdities in common experiences. The comedic angle comes from reframing normal situations to reveal their implicit silliness. Avoid abstract or overly theoretical premises that lose the ordinary reference point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gentle sarcasm (not biting)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ironic or sarcastic comments that are playful and non-hostile. The tone should nudge the audience to laugh with the performer, not at a targeted outsider. Anti-pattern: caustic sarcasm aimed at individuals/groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physicality as engine
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical movement drives and energizes the bit; gestures and posture are integral to the joke rather than decorative. Performance relies on actions as much as words; written jokes should be conceived with performable motions in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facial expressions as punctuation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facial reactions function like punctuation marks to the joke — they emphasize, underline, and time the humor. Plan micro-expressions to land beats. Anti-pattern: flat facial delivery that leaves visual cues absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical mimicry of embarrassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical mimicry of his own embarrassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mimicry and re-enactment of the performer's own awkwardness amplifies self-deprecating humor. Use reenactment to make the situation tangible and relatable. Avoid overacting that distracts from the premise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice modulation (whining, exasperation)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary vocal tone — e.g., whining, exasperated asides — to convey emotional texture and timing. Vocal choices should match the befuddled persona and support comedic beats. Anti-pattern: monotone delivery that flattens comedic dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vignette format (short story-shaped bits)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bits are structured as short, self-contained stories or vignettes that translate easily to sketch form. Each vignette contains a clear setup, complication, punchline, and optional tag. Avoid long, meandering tales without a clear payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean language — no profanity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material should avoid profanity and explicit content to maintain family-friendly mass appeal. Clean wording lets recognition and physicality carry the laugh. Anti-pattern: resorting to shock/profanity to force audience reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid politics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of political topics to preserve broad, nonpolarizing appeal. Political material undermines the universal recognition strategy and can alienate segments of the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition-based landing (not provocation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it land via recognition (not provocation)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punchlines should arise from shared recognition of everyday absurdities rather than provocation or controversy. The comedic reward comes from audience saying 'yes, me too' rather than being shocked or offended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physicality for cross-cultural appeal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying on physical comedy and visual behavior makes material accessible across cultural and linguistic boundaries. When possible, design bits whose core gag can be understood even without verbal nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material construction: story-shaped jokes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jokes should be built like mini-stories with clear narrative motion. This includes a setup that establishes the ordinary task, a complication that subverts expectations, a punchline that voices bewilderment, and tags that extend the gag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup: ordinary task attempt
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open by placing the performer in a recognizable, mundane activity. The setup stakes should be low and relatable. Avoid convoluted premises that require extensive explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complication: ordinary task confounds him
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce a small, specific obstacle or cognitive twist that foils the ordinary task and creates tension. The complication should escalate recognition and set up the punchline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punchline: bewilderment voiced
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The payoff is the performer's articulated confusion or exasperated observation about the situation. It should reframe the setup/complication in an unexpected yet accessible way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag: additional absurd realization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the punchline with one or more short tags that extend or deepen the joke by surfacing further absurdities. Tags should be tight and build momentum until a natural breathing point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric checklist (Brian Regan / Clean Anecdotal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five-question checklist: 1) Is the topic universal and mundane? 2) Is the comedian the befuddled narrator (self-deprecating)? 3) Does physicality augment the verbal? 4) Is the language clean (no profanity)? 5) Does it land via recognition (not provocation)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this compact checklist as a quick pre-performance or edit filter. If an item fails, either rework the premise/persona/delivery or discard the bit for this style. This replicates the explicit 'Rubric' given on the page.
